labels.name: United Megastore & Fan Hall
labels.desc: The flagship club shop, kit printing, ticket office and a 2,000-capacity fan hall for screenings.

labels.name: Broadcast & media centre
labels.desc: Outside-broadcast compound, press entrance and the club’s content studios.

labels.name: Manchester United Foundation
labels.desc: The Foundation’s own headquarters: offices, a community sports hall and education rooms for the schools and youth programmes it runs across Greater Manchester.

labels.name: THE FLOWERS OF MANCHESTER ARENA
labels.desc: 100,020 seats in three tiers under a single ETFE skin. 15 rose petals over a 13 + 21 spiral lattice, the wall leaning out 20° to a 60 m eave. Between skin and bowl, a seven-storey atrium of restaurants, bars and shops, open on non-matchdays.

labels.name: OLD TRAFFORD
labels.desc: The Theatre of Dreams, kept. A single tier on all four sides (about 35,000 seats) under 1990s-style cantilever roofs: home of the women’s team and the academy, and a living museum.

labels.name: Manchester United Football Ground station
labels.desc: A new station on the Liverpool–Manchester line: two island platforms 230 m long for 12-car matchday trains, step-free to the station square.

labels.name: The Busby Way · main fan walk
labels.desc: A 22 m-wide fan walk from the station to the arena’s south gate, over its own canal bridge. Statues of club legends line it; on matchdays it carries 30,000 fans an hour.

labels.name: The Trinity Walk
labels.desc: A shorter walk from the station to Old Trafford’s west forecourt.

labels.name: Botanic Garden & Munich Memorial
labels.desc: A botanic garden at the heart of the new neighbourhood, with a palm house, 23 rose beds for the 23 lives lost at Munich, and the Trinity Light.

labels.name: The Trinity Light
labels.desc: Three beams, white, blue and green, rise from the garden every evening for Charlton, Law and Best.

labels.name: Legends’ Field
labels.desc: 3 floodlit 5-a-side pitches tucked between Old Trafford’s North Stand and the canal. Former players take on supporters here on matchdays.

labels.name: Crest Plaza & south gate
labels.desc: The main arrival square: a 60 m inlaid club crest at the end of the Busby Way.

labels.name: Matchday Quarter · galleria, cinema, bars
labels.desc: Shops, restaurants, a galleria and a cinema clustered at the arena’s door, open every day of the week.

labels.name: East Stand Quarter
labels.desc: The car parks east of Sir Matt Busby Way, between the canal and the railway: a hotel and bars facing the East Stand, homes towards the tip.

labels.name: Freightliner Quarter
labels.desc: The former Freightliner terminal between the main line and the canal, now a neighbourhood of courtyard homes with a local centre of shops and cafés on Freightliner Way.

labels.name: Wharfside Quarter
labels.desc: The old Trafford Wharf sheds between Elevator Road, Trafford Wharf Road and Waterside, rebuilt: bars and restaurants on Wharfside Way facing the arena, hotels and offices behind, homes to the north.

labels.name: Canal-side homes
labels.desc: Courtyard blocks of 4–9 storeys with private gardens, stepping down towards Old Trafford.

labels.name: New neighbourhood
labels.desc: Mixed-use streets: shops and cafés at ground level near the arena, flats above, family homes towards the east. About 5,760 homes across the scheme (estimate).

labels.name: Cantona Bridge
labels.desc: A new road and cycle bridge linking the neighbourhood to John Gilbert Way.

labels.name: Avenue of Legends
labels.desc: The canal-side promenade between the two grounds, lined with trees and lamps.

labels.name: Energy centre
labels.desc: District heat pumps and the arena’s substation, serving the arena and the new homes.
